title: A remark on the Brown-Susskind conjecture
abstract: In the spirit of the Brown-Susskind conjecture, proven in \cite{haf} and \cite{li}, we study the growth of the dimension of the set of $n$-qubit unitaries which can be obtained as a product of a fixed number of $2$-qubit gates from a fixed set of pairs of qubits. We show that this dimension increases strictly when one more pair is added, for at least some choice of the $2$-qubit pairs at each step.
summary: This paper studies how the dimension of the group of achievable quantum gates grows as more 2-qubit gates are added. Using algebraic geometry, the authors prove that the dimension increases unless the gates already span the entire unitary group $U(2n)$. This provides theoretical insight into the efficiency and completeness of quantum gate decompositions.
main_problem: The paper investigates the growth rate of the dimension of the set of $n$-qubit unitaries that can be generated by multiplying a fixed number of 2-qubit quantum gates from a specified set of pairs.
main_result: The dimension of the generated set of unitaries strictly increases when an additional pair of qubits is added, provided the current set of gates does not already span the full unitary group $U(2n)$.
method: The proof relies on algebraic geometry tools, specifically the Tarski–Seidenberg theorem, to analyze the dimension of the image of the construction map, which is treated as a real-algebraic variety.
model_or_system: The system involves $n$ qubits, and the gates are constructed from a set $S$ of 2-qubit gates acting on specific pairs of qubits. The overall space is the unitary group $U(2n)$.
key_observables: The dimension of the set of achievable unitaries, $\dim(U_k)$.
important_parameters: The number of qubits ($n$), the number of gates used ($k$), and the specific pairs of qubits ($\alpha$) defining the gates.
main_assumptions: The analysis often assumes the existence of specific generating sets or relies on the gates being generated by one-parameter subgroups that are periodic and form real-algebraic subvarieties.
paper_structure: The paper builds on prior results regarding gate generation and focuses on proving a dimension growth property (Theorem 1.1) by showing that if the dimension stalls, the generated group must be the entire $U(2n)$, leading to a contradiction.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the complexity and structure of quantum gate sets, which is fundamental to understanding quantum computation feasibility and resource estimation.
